claims.text: Local surface segregation driven by differential atomic mobilities triggers the onset and progression of melting in solid FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles.
More mobile atoms preferentially enrich the nanoparticle surface.
The segregated surface is enriched in elements having lower local melting temperatures.
Surface enrichment nucleates a liquid-like premelting layer.
The liquid-like surface layer propagates inward until melting is complete.
The as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles have a random solid-solution composition.
A sub-premelting pre-anneal homogenizes the elemental distribution.
A sub-premelting pre-anneal reduces surface defects.
Defect-rich sites serve as nucleation sites for localized liquid formation.
Differences in atomic mobility among Fe, Ni, Cr, Co, and Cu cause preferential diffusion and segregation at nanoparticle surfaces at high temperature.
Local compositional enrichment produces surface regions with a reduced melting point.
Pre-annealing-induced homogenization suppresses or delays segregation during subsequent heating.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will begin premelting at a higher temperature than untreated nanoparticles.
Pre-annealed nanoparticles will fully melt at a higher temperature than untreated nanoparticles.
Untreated, as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles possess inherent surface defects.
Untreated, as-synthesized FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles possess localized elemental segregation.
In situ TEM can be used to monitor nanoparticle structural evolution during high-temperature heating.
The exact magnitude of the pre-annealing-induced transition-temperature shift is unknown.

contradictions.description: The conditions state that pre-annealing temperature and dwell time are kept identical for comparative samples, whereas the intervention and falsification design specify that only one batch is pre-annealed and the untreated control receives no such treatment.
